records.mutation: diagnose all-branches-contradictory as an over-narrow candidate list and require building the additive candidate space (including the balanced split) rather than reusing the divisor list
records.subagent_summary: Fresh sampling with the incumbent hint scored 1/8, with 2 of 8 truncating at the token cap; seven of eight rollouts enumerated only the divisor pairs of the displayed number, applied that same divisor list to both readings, concluded every branch was impossible, and then emitted an arbitrary divisor or a value they admitted was recalled or 'looks intended'. The single success was the only rollout that left the divisor list and considered a balanced additive split, so I replaced the incumbent's intersect-across-readings clause with an explicit diagnosis rule: all-branches-contradictory means the candidate space was built too narrow, and the additive reading must get its own list rather than inheriting the divisor list.

records.mutation: redirect verification to the original given relation using a solution read off the problem, since a self-manufactured test point cannot validate the map that produced it
records.subagent_summary: Seven of eight fresh rollouts were correct in 5.8k-9.1k tokens; the lone failure derived the correct locus and center/radius, then tested it on a point it had itself produced by inverting its own map (with a botched complex reciprocal), so a sound derivation appeared to contradict its own check and it looped through dozens of self-audits until the 16384-token cap without stating a result. Rounds 5-7 tried to bound or repair that loop and all lost transfer, so instead I remove its trigger: verify against the original relation with an easy exact solution read off the problem, since a test point manufactured by the very map under test cannot confirm or refute it, while keeping the setup, the no-restart rule, and early commitment.

records.mutation: make the symmetry step self-checking (confirm the slice fraction by counting the n congruent copies that tile the region) and replace open-ended scanning with a bound-plus-witness certificate
records.subagent_summary: Four of eight rollouts scored. The incumbent's wedge/anti-containment warning is working, but two failures jumped straight to an axis-aligned configuration and reported a slice fraction that was too large by a factor, then jointly reasoned the overlap wrong; the other two never reached a visible result because they kept re-deriving the setup and re-scanning rotations until the token cap. So the revision keeps the wedge and n-fold-symmetry core but makes the symmetry step verify its own fraction by counting the congruent rotated copies that tile the region, and replaces the bare stop instruction with a bound-plus-witness certificate that logically justifies halting.

records.mutation: name the residual explicitly and forbid the word difference; state that a candidate may serve many indices so the candidate count is never the answer
records.subagent_summary: Only 2 of 8 fresh rollouts were correct. Five of the six failures answered the number of available objects, each first asserting that every progression term needs its own distinct object, and one explicitly misread the hint by calling the constant step a zero-degree difference with no roots; a sixth reached the summed per-object budget and then collapsed it to a single object cap. The revision therefore renames the key quantity the residual and bans the word difference for it, and states plainly that one object may serve many indices so the object count on hand is never the count requested.

records.mutation: replace the vague second-method check with a one-number test of where an absorbed multiplicative factor belongs, plus recompute-dependent-coordinates-from-the-relation
records.subagent_summary: Only 3 of 8 fresh rollouts were correct: 3 hit the 16384-token cap mid-reduction and 2 terminated but wrong. Every failure traced to the same step -- moving an additive constant across the logarithm as a multiplicative factor on the wrong side -- which produced a different quadratic and then either a no-real-root contradiction that consumed the remaining budget or a plausible-looking wrong pair of vertices. One near-miss reduced correctly but then carried a given point's ordinate over to a new vertex instead of recomputing it from the function. So I replaced the incumbent's unspecific 'verify with a second, different method' clause, which rollouts satisfied cheaply without ever catching this slip, with a concrete one-number test of which side the absorbed factor belongs on, plus an instruction to recompute dependent coordinates from the defining relation. I kept the hint terse: every longer rewrite in rounds 1-7 lost transfer against this incumbent.

records.mutation: turn 2^(free) into a divisibility filter that rejects any 1/n or 1/n! denominator, and route which-item-in-slot-k parts through a short move PREFIX instead of full-history enumeration
records.subagent_summary: Fresh sampling with the incumbent gave 1/8; six rollouts terminated normally at 10k-16k tokens and two hit the cap while dithering, so length is secondary. Five of the eight reached the free-choice atom count on the first part and then abandoned that sample space on the later part, asserting every item is equally likely in every slot and reading off 1/n, while two never left the uniform-permutation framing at all. The revision therefore reuses the shared 2^(free) atom set as an explicit divisibility check that flags 1/n and 1/n! as proof of a false assumption, and gives a cheaper alternative to full enumeration by pinning a slot-occupancy event to a short prefix of steps whose free branches are the only ones priced.

records.mutation: reframe as isolate-one-unknown-by-annihilation with a one-time notation contract, demoting small cases to a convention check
records.subagent_summary: Fresh sampling under the incumbent scored 2 of 8, and all six failures ran to the 16384-token cap. The visible sink was not arithmetic difficulty but the incumbent's small-case-first framing itself: rollouts spent thousands of tokens renegotiating how many conditions the shrunken instance should carry, then let one symbol stand for both the summation index and the exponent, discovered the mismatch, and oscillated between readings while re-solving the same tiny system with different arithmetic each pass. The revision therefore leads with a transferable technique -- isolate the requested unknown by finding a combination that annihilates the rest -- pins the index-versus-exponent naming as a one-time contract, and demotes small cases to a single settled check for signs and off-by-one conventions so the budget goes to committing a result.

records.mutation: keep the train-preserving opening verbatim, drop the unused integrality/units tail, and replace it with a domain-neutral small-cases/invariant plus exact-arithmetic heuristic instead of more divisibility or scope advice
records.subagent_summary: All 8 fresh rollouts scored reward 1 with clean stops at 2.7-6.9k completion tokens, so train_i is saturated at 1.0 and every remaining point of J must come from transfer. Across seven rounds every append or rewrite that talked about scope labeling, gcd naming, or anti-rumination lost transfer ground while any change to the opening sentences collapsed train, and the one variant that merely deleted the unused integrality/units tail held transfer flat, which suggests the tail slot is free but that more divisibility/verification talk is off-topic for problems unlike this one. So this round keeps the opening verbatim and spends that slot on a genuinely different reusable lever the traces never exercise: reduce to small cases and extract the pattern or invariant instead of grinding a long computation, keep values exact until the end, and commit to a stated result before spending further tokens.

records.mutation: block the two observed exits from the centered form: stopping at a mere relation between the maps and then hunting extra equations, and re-expanding the solved centered form into standard powers to substitute
records.subagent_summary: Only 3 of 8 fresh rollouts were correct this round, with four running to the 16384-token cap and one terminating wrong, and the failures share a single shape: each reached the shared-center antisymmetric structure but then left it. Two collapsed it into a bare relation between the two maps, declared the remaining coefficients under-determined, and burned the budget hunting extra equations via full coefficient expansion of the composition; one rewrote the already-solved centered form into standard powers and re-added the given constant that the center already encodes, producing a wrong component. The revision therefore names both exits explicitly, asserts that fixing the center and scale finishes the problem, and requires requested inputs to be evaluated inside the centered form rather than after re-expansion.

records.mutation: name the degenerate-small-case trap (equal answers at the two smallest sizes is coincidence, push to the first size where stages differ) and make a contradicting trace kill a structural claim immediately
records.subagent_summary: 4 of 8 rollouts scored. All four failures converged on the same wrong claim, that the composite is a product of disjoint transpositions and so has period two; two of them asserted it confidently and finished, and the two token-capped ones saw their own row traces refute period two yet kept relitigating the structural claim instead of trusting the trace. Every failure was seeded by the two smallest sizes coincidentally sharing the same return count, which the incumbent already treats as a clean pattern to trust, so the revision names that degeneracy, forces a push to the first size where the stages genuinely differ, and makes a contradicting trace kill a structural claim outright.
